input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale:
Section 7.2 (first instance) imposes an MFN-style obligation on Customer, not Vendor: before engaging any other provider we must disclose any more favourable commercial offer we receive and match it for Vendor. This is unlimited as to product, duration, and comparability, with no reasonable-comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback (defined product, 12 months, carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended duty to extend Vendor better third-party terms. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The minimal fix is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would be retained.</parationale>

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2: it is an open-ended most-favoured-nation duty running against us, requiring us to hand Vendor our competitors' pricing and give Vendor a matching right before we engage anyone else. Our playbook does not accept MFN obligations on the Customer, and this term also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation in Section 7.2.
